doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

chapter: Ray Anthony and the big band end
title: The Bunny Hop as Ray Anthony's tune
summary: The Bunny Hop was Ray's own, credited to him as composer, and it sold many records as a line dance fad like the Alley Cat and Macarena.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Yeah. Was the “Bunny Hop” something that came out from someone else and he covered it? Or was it his thing?

He’s credited as being the composer. And he made a lot of money because they sold a lot of records of that. But that dance was a certain thing that was a line dance. [scats] People would hop three times. People seem to, well it was game like, it was sort of fun I guess.
Yeah. It seems like every few years another one comes along, where you had people doing that to “Alley Cat” and then the “Macarena” and some things never change I guess.
